source_review.notes: Checked all twelve references for identity, edition or version, publication date and status, publisher, and relevant scope. Official records confirm current ISO/IEC 38500:2024 edition 3, ISO/IEC/IEEE 42020:2019 as published and marked to be revised, ISO 37000:2021, and RFC 7282 as Informational. Checked publisher, journal, DOI, author, or official records for Ostrom's institutional and polycentric work, Parnas, Conway, Evans, Team Topologies 2nd edition, Nygard, and Bass-Clements-Kazman. Institutional concepts are applied as calibrated analogies rather than direct causal prescriptions for software organizations.

evidence: Defined the seven-field federation tuple, decision nodes, jurisdictions, routing classes, materially affected node set, and reserved authority before use.
Checked set, subset, cardinality, Boolean routing, implication, and counterexample language for consistent scopes.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Affected-node count is explicitly necessary context but insufficient for authority or routing.

evidence: Executed federated-decision-router under Python 3.14.4 and observed exact local, bilateral, collective, reserved-authority, and federated-review outputs with empty standard error.
Recomputed fixture cardinalities of one, two, and three affected domains against branch order and envelope flags.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The classifier is fictional and has no authority over real decisions.

evidence: Verified four-to-one support can coexist with a known material compatibility loss, refuting majority-to-safe-externality implication.
Verified two locally cost-improving history deletions can jointly eliminate recovery, refuting local-to-collective monotonic improvement.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Neither counterexample defines a universal voting rule or collective utility function.

The chapter supplies actionable routing, authority, proposal, compatibility, funding, evidence, escalation, emergency, and lifecycle practices. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.
